candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide education about health promotion/disease prevention and identify client risk factors that can be modified through lifestyle interventions.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — prediabetes lifestyle prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients with prediabetes that modest weight loss achieved through healthier eating plus regular physical activity is an evidence-based strategy to prevent or delay type 2 diabetes.

options.A: Eliminate essentially all carbohydrate foods and avoid structured physical activity until weight normalizes.
options.B: Work toward about 5%–7% weight loss through healthier eating and at least 150 minutes of physical activity each week.
options.C: Rely on vigorous exercise alone without changing eating patterns or body weight.
options.D: Wait to make lifestyle changes until blood glucose reaches the diabetes range.

candidate.rationale: CDC's National Diabetes Prevention Program is based on evidence that people with prediabetes can reduce progression to type 2 diabetes through structured lifestyle change, including healthier eating, modest weight loss of about 5%–7% of body weight, and at least 150 minutes of physical activity per week. B directly reflects those evidence-based targets. A promotes an extreme diet and defers activity; C omits the combined lifestyle approach; D delays prevention until after progression.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For adults with prediabetes and overweight, the CDC evidence-based prevention approach combines healthier eating, approximately 5%–7% weight loss, and at least 150 minutes/week of physical activity.
